'''Sylvia Frühwirth-Schnatter''' (born 21 May 1959) is an [[Austrians|Austrian]] [[statistician]] and professor of applied statistics and econometrics at the [[Vienna University of Economics and Business]]. She is known for her research in [[Bayesian analysis]]. In 2020 she was the President of the [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bayesian.org/governance/leadership/ |title=Leadership |publisher=International Society for Bayesian Analysis |access-date=February 16, 2019}}</ref>

==Biography==
Sylvia Frühwirth-Schnatter was born in 1959 in the [[Brigittenau]] district of Vienna. After attaining her doctorate in [[engineering mathematics]] from the [[TU Wien]] she held numerous academic positions, including professor of statistics at the [[Johannes Kepler University Linz]]. Since 2011, she is full professor of statistics at the [[Vienna University of Economics and Business]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://statmath.wu.ac.at/~fruehwirth/ |title=Sylvia Frühwirth-Schnatter |publisher=Vienna University of Economics and Business |access-date=February 16, 2019}}</ref> Since 2014 she is Full   Member of the Division of Humanities and the Social Sciences of the Austrian Academy of Sciences. Sylvia Frühwirth-Schnatter is married and mother of three sons.

==Research==
In her research, Sylvia Frühwirth-Schnatter inter alia explores ideas relating to [[Bayesian econometrics]], such as efficient [[Markov chain Monte Carlo]] methods and [[Bayesian analysis]] of finite [[mixture model]]s. In 2014, she co-developed a Bayesian approach to [[exploratory factor analysis]] with [[James Heckman]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Conti |first=G. |last2=Frühwirth-Schnatter |first2=S. |last3=Heckman |first3=J. J. |last4=Piatek |first4=R. |date=November 2014 |title=Bayesian exploratory factor analysis |journal=Journal of Econometrics |volume=183 |issue=1 |pages=31–57
 |doi=10.1016/j.jeconom.2014.06.008|pmid=25431517 |pmc=4242469 }}</ref>
She is a quadruple winner of the [[Vienna University of Economics and Business|WU]] Best Paper Award<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bach.wu.ac.at/d/grants/104/|title=WU Best Paper Award |publisher=Vienna University of Economics and Business |access-date=February 16, 2019}}</ref> and recipient of the DeGroot Prize<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bayesian.org/project/degroot-prize/ |title=DeGroot Prize  |publisher=International Society for Bayesian Analysis |access-date=February 16, 2019}}</ref> bestowed by the [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]] for her monograph on [[Markov chain Monte Carlo|Markov switching models]].

==Selected publications==
* Frühwirth-Schnatter, S. (2006). Finite mixture and Markov switching models. Springer Science & Business Media. {{ISBN|978-0-387-35768-3}}
* Conti, G., Frühwirth-Schnatter, S., Heckman, J. J., & Piatek, R. (2014). Bayesian exploratory factor analysis. Journal of econometrics, 183(1), 31–57.
* Frühwirth‐Schnatter, S. (1994). Data augmentation and dynamic linear models. Journal of time series analysis, 15(2), 183–202.
